description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Attribution' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Acquisition attribution — how the engine records WHERE a player came from. The signal (utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content, the ad network's click id, the referrer, the invite code) arrives with the login request and is stored as a chain of touch points on the player: the first touch is immutable, the last touch tracks win-backs, and the chain in between feeds multi-touch models. This section only tunes that recording: how many touches to keep, how long after a touch an identical signal is still considered the same click rather than a new one, and optional aliases that normalise messy source/medium values into canonical ones for analytics. Referral invites are recorded through this same mechanism as a channel, so they show up in the acquisition reports alongside paid traffic.

AppleAppStoreUrl.description: App Store listing URL. Only apps.apple.com, itunes.apple.com, appstore.com, apple.co or an itms-apps:// scheme. Empty hides the button.

AutoRedirectMobile.description: Send a phone straight to its own store instead of showing the platform picker. OFF by default, and never applied on desktop: the link is often opened on a work computer while the person plays on a phone, so there the choice must stay. WARNING - the page first waits for the click to be registered (with a short cap) and only then leaves: navigating away immediately would kill that request mid-flight and break deferred matching in exactly its main case, an ad tapped on a phone followed by a store install. Inside Telegram no redirect happens either - someone opening the link in a chat wants the mini app, not a store page.

GooglePlayUrl.description: Google Play listing URL. Validated BY HOST on save: only play.google.com, market.android.com, play.app.goo.gl or a market:// scheme. Link shorteners are refused - what hides behind them cannot be checked without following them. Empty means the platform is not configured and its button is not rendered, which is honest; a button leading somewhere wrong is not.

TelegramUrl.description: Telegram mini app or bot URL. Only t.me, telegram.me, telegram.dog or a tg:// scheme. Empty hides the button.

value.description: New value for the Attribution field.

DeferredMatchEnabled.description: Whether to match an install against a click registered earlier, when the request itself carried no signal at all. Needed where the marketing tag cannot survive the trip: the player taps an ad in a browser, goes through the app store and comes back inside the game, and the parameter is lost on the way. WARNING: this is a GUESS, not a fact - the click is matched by fingerprint (network, platform, OS version, country), and behind a mobile carrier's shared address there can be hundreds of candidates. Such touches are marked with trust level Inferred and must be shown as a separate line in reports.

DeferredMatchMaxCandidates.description: How many matching click records still count as a match. This is the only guard against false attribution: behind a carrier's shared NAT one fingerprint covers a whole building, so once the number of candidates passes this limit nothing is matched at all - guessing one out of forty is worse than attributing nobody. 0 or less means the default.

DeferredMatchTtlMinutes.description: How many minutes a registered click waits for its install before expiring. A day is the compromise: the store visit and the download take hours, but the wider the window, the more candidates share one fingerprint. 0 or less means the default. WARNING: SHORTENING this on live traffic temporarily loses some matches - the fingerprint index is read from the newest end, and a shorter TTL makes new claims expire BEFORE older ones, so a still-live older claim drops below the cut-off and is never seen. It heals itself after one old window; raising the value is always safe.

MaxHistoryEntries.description: Max length of the player's touch-point chain (UserAttributionState.History). When exceeded, MIDDLE entries are evicted — the first touch and the last touch are always kept. 0 or negative disables multi-touch entirely (only FirstTouch/LastTouch are stored). Recommended 10..50, default 20.

MediumAliases.description: Same as SourceAliases but for utm_medium — e.g. "cpc" -> "paid_search", "social-cpc" -> "paid_social".

ReengagementWindowMinutes.description: Deduplication window in minutes. A new signal arriving less than this long after the last touch is treated as a repeat click on the same link and is NOT recorded as a separate touch. 0 disables dedup — every signal becomes a new touch. Recommended 5..60, default 30.

SourceAliases.description: Optional normalisation for utm_source. Key is what the client sent (lower-cased and trimmed), value is the canonical name used in analytics — e.g. "fb" -> "facebook", "g" -> "google". Leave empty to store values exactly as received.

StoreLinks.description: Where to send a person who opened this title's link: one URL per platform, shown on the shareable invite page idosgames.com/go/{titleID}. Sits inside attribution but answers a DIFFERENT question - the rest of this section configures HOW a touch is recorded, this says WHERE to send someone. Each URL is validated BY HOST when saved; an empty one means the platform is not configured and its button is not rendered at all.
